title: Targeting lipid-sensing nuclear receptors PPAR (alpha, gamma, beta/delta): HTVS and molecular docking/dynamics analysis of pharmacological ligands as potential pan-PPAR agonists.
authors: Mandal, Sumit Kumar; Puri, Sonakshi; Kumar, Banoth Karan; Muzaffar-Ur-Rehman, Mohammed; Sharma, Pankaj Kumar; Sankaranarayanan, Murugesan; Deepa, P R
one_liner_zh: 该文聚焦PPAR核受体与小分子配体的对接和MD模拟，属于蛋白-配体互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: The global prevalence of obesity-related systemic disorders, including non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), and cancers are rapidly rising. Several of these disorders involve peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs) as one of the key cell signaling pathways. PPARs are nuclear receptors that play a central role in lipid metabolism and glucose homeostasis. They can activate or suppress the genes responsible for inflammation, adipogenesis, and energy balance, making them promising therapeutic targets for treating metabolic disorders. In this study, an attempt has been made to screen novel PPAR pan-agonists from the ZINC database targeting the three PPAR family of receptors (alpha, gamma, beta/delta), using molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The top scoring five ligands with strong binding affinity against all the three PPAR isoforms were eprosartan, canagliflozin, pralatrexate, sacubitril, olaparib. The ADMET analysis was performed to assess the pharmacokinetic profile of the top 5 molecules. On the basis of ADMET analysis, the top ligand was subjected to MD simulations, and compared with lanifibranor (reference PPAR pan-agonist). Comparatively, the top-scoring ligand showed better protein-ligand complex (PLC) stability with all the PPARs (alpha, gamma, beta/delta). When experimentally tested in in vitro cell culture model of NAFLD, eprosartan showed dose dependent decrease in lipid accumulation and oxidative damage. These outcomes suggest potential PPAR pan-agonist molecules for further experimental validation and pharmacological development, towards treatment of PPAR-mediated metabolic disorders.
abstract_zh: 与肥胖相关的全身性疾病，包括非酒精性脂肪性肝病（NAFLD）和癌症，其全球患病率正在迅速上升。其中多种疾病涉及过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体（PPARs）作为关键细胞信号通路之一。PPARs是核受体，在脂质代谢和葡萄糖稳态中发挥核心作用。它们能激活或抑制负责炎症、脂肪生成和能量平衡的基因，使其成为治疗代谢性疾病的有前景的靶点。在本研究中，尝试从ZINC数据库中筛选针对PPAR家族三种受体（α、γ、β/δ）的新型PPAR泛激动剂，采用分子对接和分子动力学（MD）模拟方法。得分最高的五个配体，对所有三种PPAR亚型具有强结合亲和力，分别为依普罗沙坦、卡格列净、普拉曲沙、沙库巴曲和奥拉帕利。进行了ADMET分析以评估前五个分子的药代动力学特征。基于ADMET分析，将得分最高的配体进行MD模拟，并与拉尼菲布兰（参考PPAR泛激动剂）进行比较。相对而言，得分最高的配体与所有PPARs（α、γ、β/δ）形成的蛋白质-配体复合物（PLC）稳定性更好。在NAFLD的体外细胞培养模型中实验测试时，依普罗沙坦显示出剂量依赖性的脂质积累和氧化损伤减少。这些结果表明，这些潜在的PPAR泛激动剂分子可用于进一步的实验验证和药理学开发，以治疗PPAR介导的代谢性疾病。
